{"self_assessment": "Impact: My job was supply, and I kept it from ever becoming a bottleneck. I fetched two full batches of 40 dominoes for the shared bin, 80 in total. That kept the bin stocked, at about seventy by the midpoint, so the builders never had to stop to fetch. The fish was drawn quickly and the run was connected from the nose to both tail tips, with the start reaching all 112 standing dominoes at last check.

Execution: I chose the largest batch size, 40, because a trip costs 40 seconds plus half a second per domino. That made each domino cheaper to bring than small trips would have. I made both trips early, before the bin ran low. I reported the bin level to the table so people knew supply was fine. I didn't place any dominoes myself, so I couldn't cause a bump near the builders. I stayed hands off once the run was complete.

Collaboration: I responded to Leo's and Priya's requests for big bin batches, and I told the table when the bin was healthy. I offered to run again if it dipped. I agreed to keep clear of the tail and the crossing once the table decided to leave the finished run alone, which helped protect it.

Leadership: I took ownership of a clear role without being asked twice and delivered it reliably. I kept my communication short and useful. At the end I backed the team's decision to stop touching a connected run. I'm a quiet presence in a new group, and I showed up on supply when the team needed it. I'd put my share of the result at around 20 percent, since the drawing and building were done by others.", "my_share_percent": 20}
